findings.title: 'Pinned binary' is recorded, not verified: no build-identity check
findings.detail: find_binary/binary_info only resolve an executable and record its sha256; self_test checks only the Zc.mat value. Any FastHenry build on PATH that reproduces a one-filament bar passes, including FastHenry2, which D0002 rejected on licence grounds. FastHenry's log prints a version banner, 'Running FastHenry 3.0wr (29Sep96, mod 031424)', that the adapter never checks. The local binary's sha256 (eaa6d6fc…) differs from D0002's recorded 15bfbcd1… (a known, documented rebuild). This meets D0002/O004's 'record sha256 + self-test' wording, but is narrower than the literal 'pinned binary'.
findings.evidence: shasum of ~/.local/bin/fasthenry = eaa6d6fc…2d14; D0002 line 38 records 15bfbcd1…7365; research/notes/o006-p4-fasthenry-feasibility.md:46 documents the discrepancy; the fake-binary self-test test shows self_test depends only on Zc.mat content
findings.suggested_check: In self_test, require the '3.0wr' / 'mod 031424' banner in the run log.

findings.title: Self-test is not enforced or recorded by solve_deck/solve_layout
findings.detail: O004 requires D0002's self-test to pass on each VM, but FHResult carries no self-test record and the solve functions never call self_test. The E004 runner must call it and store the record itself.
findings.evidence: fasthenry_run.py solve_deck lines 285-323: no self_test call; FHResult has no self-test field
findings.suggested_check: Confirm the E004 runner calls self_test() once per host and stores its dict beside the results.

findings.title: Closed-form bound in self_test is dead code
findings.detail: Once |L - 5.704| <= 1.5e-3 nH passes, L/5.695 - 1 lies in [+0.132 %, +0.184 %], always inside the 0.3 % closed-form tolerance. The second check can never fire, so it adds no protection.
findings.suggested_check: Drop it, or derive a tolerance that is not implied by the first check.

findings.title: Default timeout and memory cap are below the judged FastHenry level's projected cost
findings.detail: solve_deck defaults to timeout_s=3600 and mem_cap_mb=6000, while O004 cites P4's projection of about 10 GB and 2.4 h per run at the third (judged) level. With defaults those runs end as timeout or killed_memory and are not retried. The caller must override both.
findings.evidence: fasthenry_run.py line 286-287 defaults; O004 objective.yaml scope_in: 'P4 projected about 10 GB and 2.4 h per run at the third level'
findings.suggested_check: E004 runner review: confirm explicit timeout_s/mem_cap_mb for finest-level solves.

findings.title: An external SIGKILL (e.g. Linux OOM killer) is retried as a crash
findings.detail: Only watchdog kills are marked non-retryable. Any other signal, SIGKILL from the kernel OOM killer included, is classified 'crash' and retried up to 10 times, possibly 10 multi-hour runs on a VM. Read from code; my attempt to confirm it with a fake binary was denied by the sandbox.
findings.suggested_check: Treat SIGKILL not sent by the watchdog as non-retryable, or cap total retry wall time.

findings.title: Closed-form validation is at uniform current (10 Hz) only
findings.detail: Bar (Hoer-Love) and loop (Grover) checks run at 10-20 Hz. At the operating 10/20 MHz the tests check only plausibility bounds and multipole-vs-direct agreement. The adapter's L = Im Z/(2 pi f) path is frequency-agnostic, so this limits scope, not correctness.
findings.evidence: tests bar_deck/loop_deck use f=(10,20); end-to-end test checks 1e-9 < L < 1e-7 and m/d within 3.3e-4

findings.title: Loop-vs-Grover tolerance was fitted from a prior sweep
findings.detail: The 0.15 s/b bound comes from a sweep run before the test, not from a derivation. The added falling-error assertion still makes it a genuine convergence test. Extending to s = 0.05 mm gives err = 3.1e-4 (err/(s/b) = 0.062), still falling and inside the bound.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition of done: pytest tests/unit/test_fasthenry_run.py gave 25 passed, 0 skipped (real binary present); self_test() gave L = 5.704256 nH, pass; ruff clean. tests/unit/test_fasthenry.py still passes (55) after the exporter >2-frequency guard.

Recomputed the bar partial self-inductance with a different reduction (cross-section average of the closed-form parallel-filament mutual inductance, 2-D quadrature). It agrees with the test's Hoer-Love quadrature to ~1e-16 on 5 bars, two of them adversarial (1x5x0.3 mm short wide bar, 3x0.5x2 mm). FastHenry (direct, n = 1 and 3) agrees with it within 7.4e-7 and its DC resistance within 4.1e-6.
Re-derived Grover's rectangle formula from side self-inductances and opposite-side mutuals (thin-conductor, GMD 0.44705 s). The test's grover_rectangle is algebraically correct.
Ran the loop sweep beyond the test (s down to 0.05 mm): the relative error falls monotonically, 3.9e-3 → 3.1e-4, roughly in proportion to s.

Ran the mini-layout deck directly with each mode's flags and read FastHenry's full log: direct = 'Solution technique: LUDECOMP / Performing LU Decomposition'; multipole = 'ITERATIVE, MULTIPOLE, Order of expansion: 4, Error tolerance: 0.0001'. The multipole-vs-direct test compares genuinely different solvers.
Checked the hand arithmetic: the Ruehli closed form gives 5.6946 nH for the 10x1x1 mm bar; the recorded 5.704 nH is +0.16 %; the self-test's closed-form check is implied by its recorded-value check.

Code-read the retry semantics (range(1, max_retries+2) = 11 attempts = 1 + 10 retries, as O004 F1 requires), the crash/parse/timeout classification, that no Zc.mat is read after a nonzero exit or a signal, the proc_taskinfo struct layout (96 bytes), and ru_maxrss units per platform.
Checked D0002, D0004 and O004 for what 'pinned binary' requires: record path and sha256 plus self-test, with no hash verification required.
caveats: 'Pinned binary' holds only as 'path and sha256 recorded + self-test value reproduced'. Build identity is not verified, and the local binary's hash differs from D0002's recorded one (known rebuild).
The self-test is not run or recorded inside solve_deck/solve_layout; O004's 'self-test passed on each VM' depends on the E004 runner calling self_test().
The default timeout_s = 3600 and mem_cap_mb = 6000 must be overridden for O004's finest FastHenry level (about 2.4 h, 10 GB per P4).
Closed-form validation covers uniform current (10 Hz) only; the 10/20 MHz values are validated only by multipole-vs-direct agreement and plausibility bounds.
One adversarial probe (an external SIGKILL fake binary) was denied by the sandbox; its behaviour, a retry as a crash, is inferred from code.
